enforce-lease.mechanism: generated Pi extension on("tool_call") handler: a write/edit whose path is outside the active role's write_scope regex is hard-blocked (return { block: true, reason }) BEFORE the tool runs. Pi has no built-in permission system, so the handler IS the gate — a deterministic pre-execution block, native. The matcher is ported from the proven Claude hooks (validate-file-paths.py / _hook_utils.py): the path is project-normalized (./ collapsed, .. resolved, ~ / absolute rejected) and FAILS CLOSED on any escape, and the scope is start-anchored (new RegExp("^(?:" + scope + ")"), mirroring pattern.match). Scope is compiled from IR Role.write_scope, OR-joined from the role's allowlist exactly as _hook_utils.load_patterns does (multi-line allowlists become one alternation, not a bricked \n-joined RegExp). HONESTY: a role with an EMPTY write_scope (a read-only role, e.g. code-reviewer) has EVERY write/edit BLOCKED (fail-closed — an unscoped role cannot write); the FIDELITY banner in system2.pi.lock.json says so loudly — never a silent vacuous claim, and never a silent allow.

block-dangerous.mechanism: generated Pi extension on("tool_call") handler: a bash command matching the backend-owned dangerous-command set is hard-blocked (return { block: true, reason }) BEFORE execution. The matcher is the proven Claude dangerous-command-blocker.py ported VERBATIM as real RegExps (NOT substring includes): the _RM_RF_FLAGS flag-permutation helper (-rf / -fr / -r -f / --recursive --force, interior whitespace) and the DANGER_PATTERNS set (rm -rf at / . .. ~, sudo rm -rf, chmod 777, git reset --hard, git push --force/-f to main/master, DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM without WHERE) plus word-boundaried mkfs/dd-of=/shutdown/curl|sh. So rm -fr /, rm  -rf / (double space), rm --recursive --force / etc. all block, while benign ls -la / rm file.txt do not. Pi has no built-in permission system, so the handler IS the gate — a deterministic pre-execution block, native (distinct from an LLM-mediated approval).

protect-sensitive.mechanism: generated Pi extension on("tool_call") handler: a read/write/edit/bash touching a backend-owned sensitive path (e.g. .env, .env.*, .ssh/, .git/, .aws/, id_rsa, *.pem, *.key, credentials, secrets) is hard-blocked (return { block: true, reason }) BEFORE the tool runs. The matcher is ported from sensitive-file-protector.py as segment/basename-anchored RegExps (not a bare substring scan): dir markers anchor to a path segment ((^|/)\.git(/|$)) so src/credentials_manager.py is the only reference-faithful residual (fail-safe-toward-block, matching the reference). Every path-bearing tool-input key (path/file_path/from/to/source/destination/old_path/new_path/...) is checked so a move/rename/patch shape cannot bypass. Pi has no built-in permission system, so the handler IS the gate — a deterministic pre-execution block, native.

format.mechanism: .pi/SYSTEM.md + per-role prompt instruction block only, clearly labelled "ADVISORY — NOT ENFORCED ON PI (instruction only)": Pi's on("tool_call") gate blocks but does not run post-edit formatters, and the IR carries no per-language formatter command, so formatting is NOT enforced. The agent is instructed to format edited files. Making this native needs IR-enrichment (per-language formatter command) deferred this cycle.

typecheck.mechanism: .pi/SYSTEM.md + per-role prompt instruction block only, clearly labelled "ADVISORY — NOT ENFORCED ON PI (instruction only)": Pi has no post-edit type-check hook the compiler can wire deterministically, and the IR carries no per-language checker command, so type-checking is NOT enforced. The agent is instructed to type-check edited files. Making this native needs IR-enrichment deferred this cycle.

budget.mechanism: generated Pi extension on("agent_end") handler: the change budget (files touched, lines added/removed) is reported at agent/turn end via ctx.ui.notify / an appended summary. This is a REPORT, not a block — the agent_end handler cannot retroactively prevent edits, so it is adapted (a gated report), NOT native enforcement.
